ashwin: Heads-up — I'm seeing steady GPU memory growth on an RTX6000 when using paged KV (PagedAttention style). Start ~9.1GB, after ~15k tokens it's ~12.3GB. Paging spikes every ~2k tokens. Dumped eviction/page-table logs below.

maria: Can you paste the eviction log and kernel selection? Is this repro only on RTX6000 or also on H100/A100?

ashwin: Only on RTX6000 so far. Quick snip from the evict log: 

```
# kv_pagetable evict log (trimmed)
step 0   : alloc page 0x3f2 size=1MB owner=attn_layer_10
step 1999: page fault slot=1247 -> allocate page 0x4a1
step 2001: evict page 0x3f2 refcount=0 freed=0 note=marked_evicted
step 3999: allocate page 0x3f2 refcount=1 reused=1
step 5999: evict page 0x4a1 refcount=0 freed=0
...
# observed: many evicted pages show freed=0, free-list length grows slowly, fragmentation++
```

ashwin: The suspicious bit is `freed=0` after evict — page not actually returned to free-list. Over many cycles we accumulate allocations (and occasional new pages) leading to memory growth.

eli: Sounds like an ordering/race with async memcpy + returning page to free-list. On some GPUs/drivers a pending async DMA may keep a reference so our refcount check races. Older RTX drivers sometimes behave differently than H100.

benchbot: Profiling snapshot (short):
- kernel chosen: `attn_fwd_paged_kernel_v2` for seq=1024; fallback to `generic_attn` for seq>2048
- timings: memcpy_async wait time spikes correlate with evict ops
- per-token latency: baseline 32ms -> +18% after ~10k tokens

ashwin: Repro steps I'm using: `./run_integ.sh --model=gpt2-8k --gpu=rtx6000 --context=32k --batch=1 --paged-kv=true --tokens=20000`
Environment: CUDA 11.8, driver 470.xx, rdw-runtime@main. Also tried `KV_PAGE_EAGER_FREE=1` to force immediate free on evict.

maria: What happened with `KV_PAGE_EAGER_FREE=1`?

ashwin: It reduced the sustained growth but increased per-token latency ~7% (we sync more). Means we might be hiding a race by synchronizing.

eli: Suggestion: avoid stream-level sync in hot path. Instead change eviction to CAS the slot state and only push to free-list when CAS indicates no outstanding refs, and use event-based completion for async memcpy. Also add a debug counter pair: `evicted_pages` vs `freed_pages` to catch mismatch in prod.

maria: I'll run a long overnight job on RTX6000 and A100 (same docker/CUDA) to confirm driver vs code. If only on RTX, file bug with NV.

ashwin: Added logs to INF-2347 (ticket). Attaching `nvidia-smi` loop and dmesg tail.

ops-bot: INF-2347 created by ashwin. Priority: P2. Components: eng-runtime/kv-cache. :spiral_note_pad:

maria: Assigning to myself and eli for follow-up. I'll post results tomorrow.

ashwin: Thanks — also adding a quick patch that atomically flips `slot->state = EVICTED` before scheduling memcpy; will try to see if reduces races.

eli: If you can capture a small trace with `NVTX` around evict + memcpy + free-list push, that'll be super helpful.

ashwin: Will do.

benchbot: Reminder: if we change eviction ordering, add a bench that measures throughput for short contexts (<2k) — we can't regress common fast-paths.

maria: Agreed.

ashwin: Attached minimal repro and a tiny patch in the ticket. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
